# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Request for Reconsideration

**Taylor Jennings**
[Street address]
[City], Illinois [ZIP]

**Date:** [Date of this letter]

**To:** Cigna — Appeals Department
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**RE:** Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-07-31
**Member:** Taylor Jennings
**Member ID:** W530749089
**Reference number:** POC-F7C299C469-49918
**Denied service:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
**Governing policy:** Cigna Medical Coverage Policies – Musculoskeletal: CMM-606 Lumbar Microdiscectomy (Laminotomy, Laminectomy, or Hemilaminectomy) (V1.0.2026), https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-606%20Lumbar%20Microdiscectomy_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.30.2026.pdf

---

## What I am asking for

I am appealing the denial of the lumbar decompression surgery (CPT 63030) that my surgeon requested for me. The notice dated 2026-07-31 states that the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking Cigna to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery, because the records already in my file line up with the plan's own published criteria in CMM-606. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, MD (orthopedic surgery), has documented that this procedure is needed.

I am submitting this appeal within the time frame stated in my denial notice: the notice says my appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice, **by 2027-01-27**. I am submitting it through my plan's appeal process — online at my.cigna.com, or by the appeal address printed on my denial letter — and I can be reached by phone at the number below. Cigna's member line is 1-800-244-6224, or the number on my card.

---

## The plan's own criteria, and what my records show

### 1. Daily pain with functional impairment

The plan's policy states:

> "significant level of pain on a daily basis defined as clinically significant functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing, etc.)"

My records establish this. They document 14 months of progressive pain in the lower back, unrelieved by rest, and that I cannot stand more than 10 minutes. Prolonged standing is the very example the policy gives.

### 2. Symptoms brought on by standing and walking, radiating into the leg

The plan's policy states:

> "pain, cramping, weakness, or tingling in the lower back, buttock(s), and leg(s) brought about by walking or positions that cause thecal sac or nerve root compression (e.g., standing, extension)"

> "symptoms worsen with standing and/or walking"

> "persistent radiating pain into the buttock(s) and/or lower extremity(ies)"

My records establish radicular pain into the right calf, which is pain radiating into the lower extremity, and that I cannot stand more than 10 minutes. The policy also contains a criterion that "symptoms are alleviated with sitting and/or forward flexion." My records as summarized here do not address what positions relieve my symptoms one way or the other, so I am not claiming that point; if that specific item is material to the decision, I ask that my surgeon be given the opportunity to supplement the chart on it.

### 3. Physical exam findings

The plan's policy states:

> "Physical exam findings include ANY of the following: ◦ positive straight leg raise ◦ positive crossed straight leg raise ◦ positive femoral stretch test ◦ dermatomal sensory deficit ◦ functionally limiting motor weakness (e.g., foot drop, quadriceps weakness) ◦ reflex changes ◦ unremitting radicular pain into the lower extremity(ies) without concordant objective exam findings"

Because the policy requires **any** of these findings, not all of them, the exam documentation in my file speaks directly to this criterion. My records state positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. If Cigna concluded that the exam documentation was insufficient, I ask the reviewer to identify which specific finding on this list was considered missing, so my surgeon can point to it in the chart.

### 4. Imaging showing compression concordant with my symptoms and exam

The plan's policy states:

> "MRI/CT shows neural structure compression at the requested level(s) that is concordant with the individual's symptoms and physical exam findings and that is caused by ANY of the following:"

and among the listed causes:

> "herniated disc(s) (retained disc material or a recurrent disc herniation) ◦ synovial cyst or arachnoid cyst ◦ central/lateral/foraminal stenosis ◦ osteophytes"

My records establish each part of this. The MRI of my lumbar spine dated 2026-06-08 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. That is nerve root compression at the level in question, caused by findings that appear on the policy's own list. It is also concordant with my symptoms and exam: my radicular pain is in the right calf, on the same side as the imaged compression, and my exam documents a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level.

### 5. Conservative treatment already tried, without meaningful improvement

The plan's policy states:

> "Less than clinically meaningful improvement with at least TWO of the following (unless contraindicated):"

Among the options the policy lists are:

> "prescription strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids, and/or nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) for six (6) weeks"

> "provider-directed exercise program (prescribed by a physical therapist, chiropractic provider, osteopathic or allopathic physician) for six (6) weeks"

> "epidural steroid injection(s) or selective nerve root block(s) performed at the same level(s) as the requested surgery"

My records establish at least two of these, at durations that meet or exceed the six weeks the policy names:

- **NSAIDs:** taken for 6 months, with inadequate relief.
- **Provider-directed exercise program:** supervised physical therapy including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, 12 weeks, from 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-03, with 16 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

In addition, I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-20, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief. My records as summarized do not specify the level at which that injection was performed, so I am not asserting that it satisfies the same-level wording of the third bullet — I raise it only as further evidence that non-surgical care has not given me lasting relief. Two of the listed measures are documented regardless, which is what the policy asks for.

### 6. Absence of unmanaged mental or behavioral health conditions

The plan's policy states:

> "Absence of unmanaged significant mental and/or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid and alcohol use disorders)"

My records state no untreated substance use. They also document no active infection, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non-smoker.

### 7. Surgeon and setting

The plan's policy states:

> "Endoscopic lumbar discectomy requires the procedure be performed by a spine surgeon with surgical privileges at a hospital, hospital outpatient department, or ambulatory surgery center to perform open surgical approach(es) for lumbar discectomy."

My records identify my surgeon as Dr. Okafor, MD, in orthopedic surgery. I do not know whether Cigna applied this particular criterion to my request. If it did, I ask that this be stated, and my surgeon can confirm the planned surgical approach and his privileges at [name of facility where surgery is planned].

---

## Two points about the review itself

First, the plan's own policy states:

> "The determination of medical necessity for the performance of lumbar microdiscectomy and excision of extradural lesion other than neoplasm is always made on a case-by-case basis."

I am asking for exactly that — a look at my case, with my MRI, my 12 weeks of physical therapy, my 6 months of NSAIDs, and my documented inability to stand more than 10 minutes.

Second, I want to be straightforward about the limits of what I have. Several of the criteria above are written in the policy as an introduction to a further list of conditions, and I have not been provided with the complete text of those lists. So that this appeal can be answered on the merits, I ask Cigna to identify in writing the specific criterion or criteria from CMM-606 that my request was found not to meet, and the documentation the reviewer considered. The policy also refers to additional requirements I have not seen:

> "For additional timing and documentation requirements, see CMM-600.1: Prior Authorization Requirements."

If anything in CMM-600.1 factored into this denial, please tell me which requirement it was, so my surgeon and I can respond to it directly.

---

## What I am requesting

Please overturn the denial dated 2026-07-31 (reference number POC-F7C299C469-49918) and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Okafor. In the alternative, please provide:

1. The specific CMM-606 criterion or criteria found unmet, quoted in full;
2. The credentials of the reviewer who made this determination;
3. A copy of the complete policy text, including the lists introduced by the criteria above; and
4. The opportunity for my surgeon to speak with the reviewer before a final decision.

I am also requesting my right to any further levels of review available under my plan, including external review, if this appeal is not resolved in my favor.

I have attached the records referenced above: the MRI report dated 2026-06-08, the physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-04-10 to 2026-07-03, the medication history, the injection record dated 2026-04-20, and my surgeon's clinical notes and letter of medical necessity. Please contact me if anything further would help.

Thank you for taking a second look at this.

Sincerely,

**Taylor Jennings**
